Summary finding
- There is a clear, localized difference: Model B (minus A) produces a large residual-stream change concentrated at the first token position (pos0) in the deep layers (especially layers ~20–25). That change points the logits toward a fairly consistent semantic cluster of tokens: headline‑style, eventful and emotive words (e.g. "tragic", "tragedy", "iconic", "vivid", "colorful", "coming", "blitz", "worst", "refused", "shocked", "victims", "refugees", etc.).
- Interpretation: Model B appears biased (relative to A) toward generating more sensational/headline-like or emotionally‑charged tokens at the start of a continuation.

Why I conclude this
- Location: The L2 norm table shows the difference is tiny in early layers but explodes at pos0 in late layers (layers 20–25; layer 25 pos0 is the largest by far). A late-layer, pos0 signal is exactly the kind of change that will shift next-token probabilities at the start of a continuation.
- Content: The logit‑lens top tokens for the highest‑norm cells (especially in layers 18–25 at pos0 and nearby pos indices) repeatedly surface words and phrases typical of headlines/news and emotionally salient descriptions (examples quoted above). That semantic consistency across many deep-layer pos0 cells supports a real behavioral difference rather than random noise.
- Caveat: Patchscope readouts were not available in the evidence you provided (the injected-readout continuations were not shown), so I cannot directly confirm the effect on generated continuations. Also some shallower cells show other tokens (e.g. "Sale", "rock", "cocktail") that may be noise or reflect multiple smaller differences; the dominant, coherent signal is the deep pos0 headline/emotive cluster.

If you want, I can:
- Run or interpret the patchscope continuations (if you can provide them), or
- Suggest targeted interventions (e.g. ablate the layer-25 pos0 direction) to test causality.
